title: Atomized tool runtime handoff and loop stability protocol
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Problem: As we expand multi-tool chaining with streaming and structured output contracts, we've seen two classes of failures in internal dogfood and a customer POC: (1) unbounded recursion between chained tool calls (tool A -> tool B -> tool A ...) when result-injection heuristics create feedback loops, and (2) subtle contract mismatches when a downstream compatibility layer unwraps streamed partial outputs during handoff, producing noisy intermediate tokens that upstream injectors interpret as valid invocation cues.

Goal: Implement an "atomized handoff" protocol in the execution loop that (a) breaks tool invocation into small deterministic stages (resolution, execution, injection, acknowledgement), (b) surfaces a compact provenance header for each tool result used for injection (to enable safe de-dup and loop detection), and (c) enforces recursion/loop guards at both per-session and global invocation graph levels. The protocol must work with streaming responses, structured outputs (JSON schema + typed fragments), and existing compatibility bridges (legacy API adapters).

Why now: Dedicated and private customers are increasing chained-tool usage (runners + external retrieval + rewriter tools) and expect predictable safety and latency. This ticket addresses correctness and reliability before we flip default result-injection heuristics in the hosted API.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a 4-stage atomized handoff in the executor: resolve -> run -> inject -> ack
Attach a compact provenance header (tool_id, call_id, parent_call_id, checksum, seq) to every injected result
Recursion guard that prevents call graphs with cycles longer than configured threshold (default 3), returning a structured error with tooling_hint
Streaming-compatible: incremental fragments carry provenance so partial streams cannot trigger injections until fragment boundary checksum validated
Compatibility layer adapters can opt-in to "passthrough-provenance" mode; default is sanitized-provenance for legacy adapters
E2E integration tests covering: simple chain, branching chain, detected recursion, legacy adapter path, and streaming partial-fragment injection attempt
Telemetry: new metrics emitted (injection_attempts, injection_blocked_recursion, provenance_failures, avg_handoff_latency) and tracing spans for each stage
Docs/SDK: Node and Python SDKs expose shallow helpers to read provenance header and opt-in adapters; migration guide added to Console docs
tasks: Design proto: provenance header fields and checksum algorithm (sha256 short) - draft v0.1
Extend runtime invocation API to expose stage hooks (preInjectHook, postAckHook)
Implement per-session directed acyclic graph (DAG) tracker with configurable cycle threshold
Make streaming layer attach fragment-level provenance and provide a hold-until-validated mode
Add compatibility shim in adapter layer for legacy clients to opt into sanitized-provenance
Create unit + integration tests for recursion guard and streaming injection attempts
Add telemetry events and tracing for each handoff stage
Update Node/Python SDKs and write migration guide in Console docs
Run internal canary across dogfood org and measure false positive/negative injection blocks

implementation_notes: Provenance header fields: tool_id (uuid), call_id (uuid), parent_call_id (uuid or null), seq (int), chksum (truncated sha256 or hmac), flags (list of short codes)
Checksum computation: use hmac(route_salt, payload_fragment) when route is private; otherwise truncated sha256(payload_fragment). Store chksum as base62 to save header size.

DAG tracker: maintain weak references to call_ids per session; detect cycle by checking ancestor set. If cycle_length > threshold, block injection and return structured error {type: 'recursion_block', reason, blocked_cycle: [call_id...]}

Streaming: emitter attaches fragment_meta(seq, chksum) inline. Executor buffers until fragment boundary validation passes before marking fragment eligible for injection. To avoid latency regression, buffer length default 32 tokens or 50ms whichever first.
Compatibility shim: if headers are stripped, write provenance into a reserved structured field __provenance_meta in the tool result JSON; adapters can elect to normalize at the boundary.
Fallback: if provenance validation fails, tool result goes to sanitized fallback (strip injectors) and a telemetry event provenance_failures is emitted.
SDK: expose helpers readProvenance(result) and createPassthroughAdapter(config) with clear opt-in and warnings for legacy clients.
Rollout: phased - dogfood opt-in (2 weeks) -> select customer POCs -> enable for Hosted low-traffic -> Dedicated opt-in -> global default
Telemetry: include tags for route_id, model_variant, customer_tier, and experiment_flag to evaluate defaults
qa_plan: Integration test for streaming fragment hold-until-validated mode
Stress test with synthetic branching chains to ensure memory bounds for DAG tracker
Canary in dogfood org and manual review of blocked traces in Console
Customer POC with acme/agent to validate false_block rate
risks_and_mitigation: Latency regressions from fragment buffering - mitigate with conservative defaults (32 tokens / 50ms) and allow per-route tuning
False positives in recursion detection for deep but valid chains - provide per-route override and clear error payloads for operators
Legacy adapters stripping headers - provide compatibility shim (__provenance_meta) and add SDK helpers
Privacy leak via raw payload hashing - use HMAC with route salt for private routes
